The **DateTime** standard library parses dates and computes durations — useful
whenever a check involves timing or timestamps. `Convert Date` parses a date
string; `Subtract Date From Date` returns the gap, in seconds by default.

## Task 1 — Compute a duration between two times

**Goal:** create `checks/datetime.robot` that parses two times twenty minutes
apart and asserts the gap between them in seconds.

Here is the same calculation over a different, shorter interval. Adapt it.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    DateTime

*** Test Cases ***
Measure Minutes Between Times
    ${start}=    Convert Date    2026-01-15 09:00:00
    ${end}=      Convert Date    2026-01-15 09:05:00
    ${gap}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${end}    ${start}
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${gap}    300
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite imports `DateTime` and defines `Compute A Duration`.

<!-- hint -->
Parse both times with `Convert Date`, e.g.
`Convert Date    2026-07-01 08:00:00` and `Convert Date    2026-07-01 08:20:00`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
`Subtract Date From Date    ${end}    ${start}` gives the gap in seconds. Twenty
minutes is `1200` — assert `Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${elapsed}    1200`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    DateTime

*** Test Cases ***
Compute A Duration
    ${start}=    Convert Date    2026-07-01 08:00:00
    ${end}=      Convert Date    2026-07-01 08:20:00
    ${elapsed}=    Subtract Date From Date    ${end}    ${start}
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${elapsed}    1200
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the computed duration is 1200 seconds.
